taxonomy.evidence: Exact normalized paragraph text repeats within a report.
The same accepted interpretation unit is paraphrased repeatedly inside one report.
The same accepted interpretation unit is fully restated across multiple sections.
Legacy quality checks do not identify generic filler; this does not establish paid-value quality.
Available sections reuse existing units without a section-level new-information eligibility gate.
No frozen technical-to-customer content ratio exists in legacy SMR.
Priority does not materially suppress repeated lower-information paragraphs.
Different intent variants within the same method/locale produce the same paragraph sequence.
Method-specific glossary dominance is not measured by the legacy gate.
Legacy paragraphs are lineage-bound; traceability itself is not the current failure.
Legacy reports exceed the R2 audit density threshold of 24 body paragraphs without information-gain gating.
Legacy review CSS has a breakpoint but no mobile reading-layout contract or wall-of-text gate.
Legacy review CSS has print rules but no widow/orphan, clipped-chart, or UI-control contract.
Length is materially inflated by repeated explanation rather than new claims or relations.
The legacy campaign varies locale/intent over one underlying authority per method, so it is not structural-diversity evidence.
